summary: Joseph Hogue, CFA — 'My New Favorite Stocks for AI Growth AND Income' (published 29 Sep 2026). Pitch: income investors no longer have to choose between AI-driven growth and cash flow. Hogue argues new YieldMax option-income ETFs let holders capture semiconductor upside while converting industry volatility into distributions. He walks through four: (1) CHPY — YieldMax Semiconductor Portfolio Options Income ETF, holding 15-30 semiconductor names and using a call-spread strategy targeting ~40% annualized distribution with weekly payouts (range this year $0.38-$0.71/share). (2) SOXY — the YieldMax Target 12 semiconductor fund, a growth-leaning counterpart targeting 12% income so more upside stays in the portfolio (monthly payouts, $0.65 to over $1/share this year). (3) AMDY — a single-stock AMD options-income ETF for a tactical overweight on AMD, which he says he bought early last year and has since cashed. (4) NVDY — the single-stock Nvidia version targeting a 47% distribution rate. Suggested builds: max income = 70% CHPY / 15% NVDY / 15% AMDY; income-plus-growth = 50% SOXY / 25% AMDY / 25% NVDY. He flags the risks: distributions fluctuate with premiums and volatility, and income is never guaranteed. Calls made: CHPY BUY (~40% target), SOXY BUY (12% target), AMDY BUY, NVDY BUY (47% target). Other tickers discussed: MU (up ~1,200% over 5 years), MRVL (~+400%), NVDA (10x), ARM — all mentioned only as semiconductor theme leaders held inside the ETFs, not as direct calls. Note: captions rendered the second fund's ticker as 'SOX Y', with garbled repeats as 'SOXW' and 'SOXL' later in the video — the described product is consistently the Target 12 fund. The video is sponsored by YieldMax, disclosed in-video.
